svg.title: The route of the glory
svg.desc: A plate in three parts on one west-to-east profile of the temple, its east gate, the city wall, the Kidron valley and the mountain east of the city. Above, Ezekiel 8-11, drawn solid: the glory goes from the cherub to the threshold (Ezekiel 9:3; 10:4), out to the east gate (Ezekiel 10:18-19), and stands on the mountain east of the city (Ezekiel 11:22-23). In the middle, Ezekiel 43-44, drawn solid: the glory comes from the east with a sound like many waters (Ezekiel 43:2), enters by the east gate (Ezekiel 43:4), fills the house, the place of the LORD's throne (Ezekiel 43:5-7), and the east gate is shut because the LORD has entered by it (Ezekiel 44:1-2). Zechariah 14:4 names the mountain: the Mount of Olives. Below, in a dashed frame because no New Testament writer draws the link, the road Jesus walked: down the Mount of Olives weeping over the city (Luke 19:37, 41-44), 'your house is left to you desolate' (Matthew 23:38-39), out of the temple to the Mount of Olives (Matthew 24:1-3), taken up from Olivet (Acts 1:9-12), and his feet standing on the Mount of Olives (Zechariah 14:4). The plate closes with Ezekiel 43:7.
svg.text: Ezekiel 8-11 and 43-44, and the road Jesus walked
EZEKIEL 8-11 · THE GLORY GOES OUT (592 BC)
the mountain east of the city
EZEKIEL 43-44 · THE GLORY COMES BACK (573 BC)
the mountain east of the city
From the cherub to the threshold
Stood on the mountain east of the city
Comes from the east, “like the sound of many waters”
Enters by the gate facing east
Fills the house: “the place of my throne”
The east gate shut: “the LORD… has entered by it”
A PATTERN · THE ROAD JESUS WALKED
Comes down the Mount of Olives and weeps over the city
“Your house is left to you desolate… until you say…”
Leaves the temple and sits on the Mount of Olives
Taken up from “the mount called Olivet”
“His feet shall stand on the Mount of Olives”
Dashed: the events are stated; their link to Ezekiel 11:23 and 43:2 is a pattern no
New Testament writer draws. E is still to come.
“This is the place of my throne and the place of the soles of my feet,
where I will dwell in the midst of the people of Israel forever.”
After the manner of Clarence Larkin · the-way.lewy.au
